definitions.title: How are these metrics calculated?
definitions.session: Service session: starts at the customer's first message when no session is open (after 24 h of silence since the last reply, or after the conversation was resolved). An unanswered session stays open until someone replies.
definitions.firstResponse: First response: time from the session start to the first reply from a person or the AI. First human response only counts replies from people. Internal notes and system messages don't count. P90: 90% of sessions were answered within that time.
definitions.sla: Response target: {minutes} minutes. Answered sessions count, plus sessions still unanswered past the target.
definitions.resolution: Resolution: from the session start until it was resolved. Source used:
definitions.unanswered: Waiting for a reply: conversations not closed whose last message (excluding internal notes) is from the customer.

attention.short: How fast and how well you answer your customers.
attention.intro: This section measures your customers' experience when they write: how many new conversations came in, how long until the first reply (AI or a person), how many were answered within your target time and how long they took to resolve.
attention.how: Look first at the first reply and the share within target: that's what customers feel most. «Waiting for a reply now» are customers who wrote and nobody has answered yet.

volume.short: How many messages you get and send, by day, channel and hour.
volume.intro: This section shows the workload: how many messages customers sent, how many your team and the AI sent, on which days and channels, and the hours when demand peaks.
volume.how: Use the peak-hours map to decide when to add people. If a channel grows a lot, consider giving it its own AI agent or inbox group.

team.short: Who served: people, AI or both, and each agent's performance.
team.intro: This section compares your team's work with the AI's: how many replies each gave, which conversations the AI solved alone, which went to a person and how each team member performed.
team.how: A good sign is the AI solving most simple questions alone and handed-over chats reaching a person fast. Check each agent's median first reply to spot delays.

ai.short: What the AI did, how often it handed over and its cost.
ai.intro: This section sums up your AI agents' work: replies sent, conversations involved, share handed to a person and the AI model's internal cost.
ai.how: A high handover rate may mean the AI lacks information: complete the FAQs, catalog or agent instructions. The internal cost is a reference; you pay with credits.

sales.short: Orders, revenue, bookings and how many chats end in a purchase.
sales.intro: This section shows the period's commercial results: orders created and their status, total sold, bookings and conversion — how many conversations ended in an order.
sales.how: Conversion tells you how well chats turn into sales. If many orders stay pending or cancelled, review follow-ups and payment methods.

meta.short: WhatsApp messages Meta bills and their estimated cost.
meta.intro: Since October 1, 2026 Meta bills every reply sent on WhatsApp. Each number gets 1,000 free replies a month and templates are always billed. This section estimates what Meta will bill this month, per number and message type.
meta.how: If a number nears the free limit, make sure your WhatsApp Business account has a payment method: without one, Meta stops delivering replies past the limit. The real invoice is in your WhatsApp Manager.
